name: Executive order of September 22, 1866 setting apart a reservation at Shoalwater Bay
citation: Executive order of September 22, 1866 (Royce schedule p. 842)
nations: Shoalwater Bay Indian Tribe; Royce names the Puyallup and others
promises: Not a treaty. Royce records that the President withdrew parts of sections 2 and 3, T. 14 N., R. 11 W., for a reservation at Shoalwater Bay (Royce p. 842, area 493).
Royce (p. 833) records that the Chehalis, Chinook and other tribes of this country were assigned first one small reserve (Chehalis) and afterward another at Shoalwater Bay.
today: No court, claims-commission, Act of Congress or government finding about the Shoalwater Bay reservation land was found in this pass.

sources.title: Charles C. Royce, Indian Land Cessions in the United States (18th Annual Report of the Bureau of American Ethnology, 1899), schedule pp. 842-843

openQuestions: treaties.json names this entry for the Puyallup and gives the Puyallup Tribe as present-day tribe. Royce's tribe column reads 'Puyallup and others', but the order sets apart the Shoalwater Bay reservation on Shoalwater (Willapa) Bay in south-western Washington, the home of the Shoalwater Bay Indian Tribe. Not edited.
Indian Claims Commission dockets of the Chinook (234) and Chehalis concern aboriginal title, not this reservation; not read in full.
The Shoalwater Bay Indian Tribe's own account was not located in this pass.

Audit 2026-11-08 (round 12): 'north-western Washington' corrected to south-western: Shoalwater Bay lies on the Pacific coast of south-western Washington, and Royce's township (T. 14 N., R. 11 W.) is there. Royce p. 842 entry (Puyallup and others; parts of secs. 2 and 3, T. 14 N., R. 11 W.) confirmed.
